http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.label: UnitSymbol
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.comment:
The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole.
			Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single-letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol.
			To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3  or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "°" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol.
			Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units.
			The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.label: UnitMultiplier
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.comment:
The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.  When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single-character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type.
			For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "Þ" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "kÞ".
			For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g".  If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram.  As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "Þ", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "mÞ", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment:
A value and normal value associated with a specific kind of limit.
			The sub class value and normalValue attributes vary inversely to the associated OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short).
			If a particular piece of equipment has multiple operational limits of the same kind (apparent power, current, etc.), the limit with the greatest acceptableDuration shall have the smallest limit value and the limit with the smallest acceptableDuration shall have the largest limit value.  Note: A large current can only be allowed to flow through a piece of equipment for a short duration without causing damage, but a lesser current can be allowed to flow for a longer duration.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.label: OverlappingZone
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.comment: A collection of all the overlapping cross border assessed elements which have the same sets of impacted and impacting regions.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorr.label: PowerTransferCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorr.comment: A power transfer corridor is defined as a set of circuits (transmission lines or transformers) separating two portions of the power system, or a subset of circuits exposed to a substantial portion of the transmission exchange between two parts of the system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#Region.label: Region

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RemedialAction.label: RemedialAction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RemedialAction.comment: Remedial action describes one or more actions that can be performed on a given power system model situation to eliminate one or more identified breaches of constraints. The remedial action can be costly, and have a cost characteristic, or non costly.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.label: Date
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.comment: Date as "yyyy-mm-dd", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-dd(+/-)hh:mm".

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DateTime.label: DateTime
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DateTime.comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.label: IRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
			The primitive is serialized as rdf:resource in RDFXML.
			IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
			IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
			IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringFixedLanguage
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.
			The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringIRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
			The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.
			IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
			IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
			IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.label: URL
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.comment: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL), colloquially termed a web address, is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. A URL is a specific type of Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), although many people use the two terms interchangeably.URLs occur most commonly to reference web pages (http), but are also used for file transfer (ftp), email (mailto), database access (JDBC), and many other applications.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#AvailabilityPower.label: AvailabilityPowerSystemFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#AvailabilityPower.comment: Availability power system function describes the power system function that has a non-normal availability in the associated availability schedule. The availability of the function is needed as part of a power flow solution. This function is the cause and not the effect of the availability, if the effect can be calculated through power flow. For instance if only the step-up transformer for a generator is not available, the power flow will calculate that the generator is de-energized (outage). If both are tagged as not available it will not be possible to investigate remedial action for connecting the generator. It is expected that the power flow function is able to perform simple topology changes affected by a function taken out of service, e.g. open switches on both end of a ACLineSegment when the ACLineSegment is taken out of service. More complex changes, like change regulation set point, must be described in the linked GridStateAlterationCollection.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#AvailabilityRemed.comment: Availability remedial action scheme serves for associating a remedial action scheme with an availability schedule. http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#AvailabilitySched.label: AvailabilitySchedule

A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Duration.comment: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment:
A value and normal value associated with a specific kind of limit. 
The sub class value and normalValue attributes vary inversely to the associated OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short).  
If a particular piece of equipment has multiple operational limits of the same kind (apparent power, current, etc.), the limit with the greatest acceptableDuration shall have the smallest limit value and the limit with the smallest acceptableDuration shall have the largest limit value.  Note: A large current can only be allowed to flow through a piece of equipment for a short duration without causing damage, but a lesser current can be allowed to flow for a longer duration.

A Remedial Action Scheme consists of one or more stages that can trigger and execute a protection action.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.label: UnitMultiplier
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.comment:
The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.  When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single-character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type. 

For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "Þ" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "kÞ".

For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g".  If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram.  As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "Þ", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "mÞ", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.label: UnitSymbol
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.comment:
The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole. 
Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single-letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol.
To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3  or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "°" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol.
Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units. 
The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.label: Date
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.comment: Date as "yyyy-mm-dd", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-dd(+/-)hh:mm".

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.label: IRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as rdf:resource in RDFXML.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringIRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringFixedLanguage
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.label: URL
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.comment: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL), colloquially termed a web address, is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. A URL is a specific type of Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), although many people use the two terms interchangeably.URLs occur most commonly to reference web pages (http), but are also used for file transfer (ftp), email (mailto), database access (JDBC), and many other applications.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.label: UnitSymbol
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.comment:
The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole. 
Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single-letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol.
To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3  or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "°" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol.
Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units. 
The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.label: UnitMultiplier
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.comment:
The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.  When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single-character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type. 

For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "Þ" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "kÞ".

For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g".  If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram.  As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "Þ", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "mÞ", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.label: IRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as rdf:resource in RDFXML.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model
http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment:
A Model is a collection of data describing instances, objects or entities, real or computed. In the context of CIM the semantics of the data is defined by profiles. Hence a model can contain equipment data, power flow initial values, power flow results etc.
The Model class describes the header content that is the same for the FullModel and the DifferenceModel. A Model is identified by an rdf:about attribute. The rdf:about attribute uniquely describes the model data and not the CIMXML document. A new rdf:about identification is generated for created documents only when the model data has changed. A repeated creation of documents from unchanged model data shall have the same rdf:about identification as previous document generated from the same model data.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.label: UnitSymbol
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitSymbol.comment:
The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole. 
Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single-letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol.
To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3  or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "°" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol.
Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units. 
The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.label: UnitMultiplier
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#UnitMultiplier.comment:
The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.  When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single-character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type. 

For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "Þ" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "kÞ".

For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g".  If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram.  As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "Þ", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "mÞ", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ClosedDistributio.label: ClosedDistributionSystemOperator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ClosedDistributio.comment: A system operator which distributes electricity (or gas) within a geographically confined industrial, commercial or shared services and does not supply household customers.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CompensatorContro.label: CompensatorController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CompensatorContro.comment: Compensator controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the use of the compensators.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ConductingEqui.label: ConductingEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ConductingEqui.comment: The parts of the AC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through terminals.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ConnectivityNo.label: ConnectivityNodeContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ConnectivityNo.comment: A base class for all objects that may contain connectivity nodes or topological nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ControlArea.label: ControlArea
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ControlArea.comment:
A control area is a grouping of generating units and/or loads and a cutset of tie lines (as terminals) which may be used for a variety of purposes including automatic generation control, power flow solution area interchange control specification, and input to load forecasting. All generation and load within the area defined by the terminals on the border are considered in the area interchange control. Note that any number of overlapping control area specifications can be superimposed on the physical model. The following general principles apply to ControlArea:
1.  The control area orientation for net interchange is positive for an import, negative for an export.
2.  The control area net interchange is determined by summing flows in Terminals. The Terminals are identified by creating a set of TieFlow objects associated with a ControlArea object. Each TieFlow object identifies one Terminal.
3.  In a single network model, a tie between two control areas must be modelled in both control area specifications, such that the two representations of the tie flow sum to zero.
4.  The normal orientation of Terminal flow is positive for flow into the conducting equipment that owns the Terminal. (i.e. flow from a bus into a device is positive.) However, the orientation of each flow in the control area specification must align with the control area convention, i.e. import is positive. If the orientation of the Terminal flow referenced by a TieFlow is positive into the control area, then this is confirmed by setting TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag TRUE. If not, the orientation must be reversed by setting the TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag FALSE.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ControlFunctionBl.label: ControlFunctionBlock
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ControlFunctionBl.comment: Control function block is a function block that contains an algorithm for controlling the equipment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentControlFun.label: CurrentControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentControlFun.comment: Current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopContr.label: CurrentDroopControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopContr.comment: Current droop control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target current.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#CurrentFlow.label: CurrentFlow
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#CurrentFlow.comment: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopOverr.label: CurrentDroopOverride
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopOverr.comment:
Current droop override uses the following logic:
- When the current exceeds a threshold the device executes the following transitions: 1) When injecting an inductive voltage or in monitoring mode the device tends to inject a voltage proportional to the difference between the line current and the aforementioned threshold. 2) When injecting a capacitive voltage the device transitions to monitoring mode. 
- If the aforementioned proportional voltage is lower than the initial one, the voltage injection remains unchanged. 
Current droop override is not applied when the device operates in currentDroop mode.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Curve.label: Curve
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Curve.comment: A multi-purpose curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and dependent (Y-axis) variables.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#CurveData.label: CurveData
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#CurveData.comment: Multi-purpose data points for defining a curve.  The use of this generic class is discouraged if a more specific class can be used to specify the X and Y axis values along with their specific data types.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCBreaker.label: DCBreaker
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCBreaker.comment: A breaker within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCBusbar.label: DCBusbar
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCBusbar.comment: A busbar within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCChopper.label: DCChopper
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCChopper.comment: Low resistance equipment used in the internal DC circuit to balance voltages. It has typically positive and negative pole terminals and a ground.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCConductingEq.label: DCConductingEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCConductingEq.comment: The parts of the DC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through DC terminals.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCConverterUni.label: DCConverterUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCConverterUni.comment: Indivisible operative unit comprising all equipment between the point of common coupling on the AC side and the point of common coupling – DC side, essentially one or more converters, together with one or more converter transformers, converter control equipment, essential protective and switching devices and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCCurrentControlF.label: DCCurrentControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCCurrentControlF.comment: DC current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PU.label: PU
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PU.comment: Per Unit - a positive or negative value referred to a defined base. Values typically range from -10 to +10.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCDisconnector.label: DCDisconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCDisconnector.comment: A disconnector within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCEquipmentCon.label: DCEquipmentContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCEquipmentCon.comment: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containment of DC as well as AC equipment. The class differ from the EquipmentContaner for AC in that it may also contain DCNode-s. Hence it can contain both AC and DC equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCGround.label: DCGround
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCGround.comment: A ground within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCLine.label: DCLine
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCLine.comment: Overhead lines and/or cables connecting two or more HVDC substations.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCLineSegment.label: DCLineSegment
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCLineSegment.comment: A wire or combination of wires not insulated from one another, with consistent electrical characteristics, used to carry direct current between points in the DC region of the power system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCPole.label: DCPole
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCPole.comment: The direct current (DC) pole is the circuit which includes converter units from both sides and the relevant direct current line. This forms the smallest unit of transmission control.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCSeriesDevice.label: DCSeriesDevice
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCSeriesDevice.comment: A series device within the DC system, typically a reactor used for filtering or smoothing.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCShunt.label: DCShunt
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCShunt.comment: A shunt device within the DC system, typically used for filtering.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCSwitch.label: DCSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DCSwitch.comment: A switch within the DC system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCTieCorridor.label: DCTieCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCTieCorridor.comment: A collection of one or more direct current poles that connect two different control areas.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ActivePower.label: ActivePower
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ActivePower.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCVoltageControlF.label: DCVoltageControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DCVoltageControlF.comment: DC voltage control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCirc.label: DirectCurrentCircuit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCirc.comment: A direct current circuit is a circuit consists of direct current equipment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCont.label: DirectCurrentController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCont.comment: Power flow controller for direct current that can be used in high-voltage direct current grids and for low-voltage direct current microgrids. It uses a high-frequency isolated dc-dc converter cascaded with a controllable full-bridge inverter that creates a small bipolar voltage in series with the line. The controller can control the power and compensate for accumulated voltage drop in a distribution line.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSyst.label: DirectCurrentSystemOperator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSyst.comment: System operator of the direct current pole. There are typically one or two system operators that are operating either the control area at one side or the control areas at both sides of the direct current pole. In some cases it is operated by an operator from the connected control areas.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DistributionSyste.label: DistributionSystemOperator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DistributionSyste.comment: A system operator that is responsible for operating of energy distribution network from transmission level down to low voltage levels including the connection to household.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DurationOverloadL.label: DurationOverloadLimitCurve
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#DurationOverloadL.comment:
A curve or functional relationship between
- the overload duration independent variable (X-axis), and 
- temporary overloading (TATL) limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyAlignmentCo.label: EnergyAlignmentCoordinator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyAlignmentCo.comment: A role that is responsible for alignment of forecast and schedule energy to a given energy coordination region.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockCompon.label: EnergyBlockComponent
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockCompon.comment: The energy block component is an energy component where the energy group active power is distributed according to the energy block order of each energy component in an energy group.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockOrder.label: EnergyBlockOrder
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockOrder.comment: The energy block order is a block (an amount) of active power that forms the sequence of active power orders that are going to be distributed to an energy block component.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Integer.label: Integer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Integer.comment: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyComponent.label: EnergyComponent
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyComponent.comment: The energy component is an active power component for an energy producer or a consumer that has the same energy characteristic, e.g. fuel type and technology.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:EnergyComponent:associations
extraRules.description: The EnergyComponent shall be associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer or HydroPump.
extraRules.message: EnergyComponent is not associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer or HydroPump.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EnergyConnecti.label: EnergyConnection
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EnergyConnecti.comment: A connection of energy generation or consumption on the power system model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EnergyConsumer.label: EnergyConsumer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EnergyConsumer.comment:
Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.
EnergyConsumer.pfixed, .qfixed, .pfixedPct and .qfixedPct have meaning only if there is no LoadResponseCharacteristic associated with EnergyConsumer or if LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is set to False.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyCoordinatio.label: EnergyCoordinationRegion
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyCoordinatio.comment: A region that has a common organisation or a service that is responsible for alignment of forecast and scheduling of energy.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyGroup.label: EnergyGroup
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyGroup.comment: An energy group is an aggregation of energy components which have the same energy characteristic, e.g. fuel type and technology. It can be used to allocate energy.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyTypeReferen.label: EnergyTypeReference
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EnergyTypeReferen.comment: An energy type reference refers to an energy characteristic that is needed for reporting, e.g. European Energy Certificate System (EECS). The kind of energy should be possible to be linked with different type of energy forecast, e.g. wind production for a given area based on wind forecast.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Equipment.label: Equipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Equipment.comment: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EquipmentConta.label: EquipmentContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EquipmentConta.comment: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containing equipment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EquipmentControll.label: EquipmentController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#EquipmentControll.comment: Equipment controller is an automation function that can control one or multiple equipment function to achieve all the targets inside the given tolerance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EquivalentInje.label: EquivalentInjection
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#EquivalentInje.comment: This class represents equivalent injections (generation or load).  Voltage regulation is allowed only at the point of connection.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ExceptionalPowerT.label: ExceptionalPowerTransferCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ExceptionalPowerT.comment: Potential power transfer corridor that can be triggered by equipment which changes its in service status or it is operating in an island.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FacilityPlantCont.label: FacilityPlantController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FacilityPlantCont.comment: Facility plant controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the facility plant.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FACTSEquipment.label: FACTSEquipment
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FACTSEquipment.comment: Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System regulating equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Reactance.label: Reactance
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Reactance.comment: Reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Feeder.label: Feeder
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Feeder.comment:
A collection of equipment for organizational purposes, used for grouping distribution resources.
The organization a feeder does not necessarily reflect connectivity or current operation state.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FlexibleEnergyUni.label: FlexibleEnergyUnit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FlexibleEnergyUni.comment: Flexible consumer or embedded producer of energy. The unit cannot be a net producer.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#FossilFuel.label: FossilFuel
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#FossilFuel.comment: The fossil fuel consumed by the non-nuclear thermal generating unit.   For example, coal, oil, gas, etc.   These are the specific fuels that the generating unit can consume.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FuelStorage.label: FuelStorage
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FuelStorage.comment: Fuel storage. e.g. pile of coal that can be shared between multiple thermal generating units.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionBlock.label: FunctionBlock
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionBlock.comment: Function block is a function described as a set of elementary blocks. The blocks describe the function between input variables and output variables.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionInputVari.label: FunctionInputVariable
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionInputVari.comment: Functional input variable defines the domain of the function.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionOutputVar.label: FunctionOutputVariable
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FunctionOutputVar.comment: Functional output variable defines the codomain of the function.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GateInputPin.label: GateInputPin
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GateInputPin.comment: Input pin for a logical gate. The condition described in the input pin gives a logical true or false. The result from measurement and calculation are converted to a true or false.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LogicalOperatorsK.label: LogicalOperatorsKind
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LogicalOperatorsK.comment: Kinds of logical operators for comparison.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Duration.label: Duration
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Duration.comment: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#GeneratingUnit.label: GeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#GeneratingUnit.comment: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

extraRules.name: DanglingReferences-ERGeneratingUnit
extraRules.description: The OperationalLimits is the link with IGMs/CGMs and should have a valid mRID on the RA class.
extraRules.message: Dangling reference is present in the model. The Conduct EQ mRID: {?value} of the class ID: {$this}.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Currency.label: Currency
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Currency.comment: Monetary currencies.  ISO 4217 standard including 3-character currency code.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Decimal.label: Decimal
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Decimal.comment: Decimal is the base-10 notational system for representing real numbers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ActivePowerCha.label: ActivePowerChangeRate
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ActivePowerCha.comment: Rate of change of active power per time.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GeothermalGenerat.label: GeothermalGeneratingUnit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GeothermalGenerat.comment: Generating unit that is generating electrical power from geothermal energy.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#HydroPowerPlan.label: HydroPowerPlant
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#HydroPowerPlan.comment: A hydro power station which can generate or pump. When generating, the generator turbines receive water from an upper reservoir. When pumping, the pumps receive their water from a lower reservoir.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#HydroPump.label: HydroPump
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#HydroPump.comment: A synchronous motor-driven pump, typically associated with a pumped storage plant.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#IdentifiedObje.label: IdentifiedObject
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#IdentifiedObje.comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ImpedanceControlF.label: ImpedanceControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ImpedanceControlF.comment: Impedance control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target impedance.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InfeedLimit.label: InfeedLimit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InfeedLimit.comment: Infeed limit set constraints fed in to the network by two or more terminals.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InfeedTerminal.label: InfeedTerminal
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InfeedTerminal.comment: Infeed terminal defines the terminals that are linked to an infeed limit.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InjectionControll.label: InjectionController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#InjectionControll.comment: Injection controller is controlling the equipment which represents an injection or an external network.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LimitDependencyCu.label: LimitDependencyCurve
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LimitDependencyCu.comment: A curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Line.label: Line
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Line.comment: Contains equipment beyond a substation belonging to a power transmission line.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LineCircuit.label: LineCircuit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LineCircuit.comment: A line circuit is a circuit that has at least one ACLineSegment and may or may not include related switching and/or auxiliary equipment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.label: LoadFrequencyControlArea
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.comment: A part of a synchronous area or an entire synchronous area, physically demarcated by points of measurement at interconnectors to other load frequency control (LFC) areas, operated by one or more TSOs fulfilling the obligations of load-frequency control.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.label: LoadFrequencyControlBlock
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.comment: A part of a synchronous area or an entire synchronous area, physically demarcated by points of measurement at interconnectors to other load frequency control (LFC) blocks, consisting of one or more LFC areas, operated by one or more TSOs fulfilling the obligations of load-frequency control.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.label: LoadFrequencyControlOperator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyCont.comment: A role that is responsible for operational security by operating the load frequency control (LFC) mechanism.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LossCurve.label: LossCurve
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#LossCurve.comment: Represents the losses in the equipment due to operation position.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ModularStaticSync.label: ModularStaticSynchronousSeriesCompensator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ModularStaticSync.comment: Modular static synchronous series compensator (MSSSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment which consists of solid-state voltage source inverter connected in series with a transmission line. This is similar to static synchronous series compensator (SSSC), but without injection transformer. This enables the MSSSC to be truly modular with the ability to simply install a number of equipment in series to provide a desired maximum level of impedance. MSSSC can be dispersed into multiple location in a circuit working collectively under the same controller scheme.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment:
A value and normal value associated with a specific kind of limit. 
The sub class value and normalValue attributes vary inversely to the associated OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short).  
If a particular piece of equipment has multiple operational limits of the same kind (apparent power, current, etc.), the limit with the greatest acceptableDuration shall have the smallest limit value and the limit with the smallest acceptableDuration shall have the largest limit value.  Note: A large current can only be allowed to flow through a piece of equipment for a short duration without causing damage, but a lesser current can be allowed to flow for a longer duration.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimitSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment: A set of limits associated with equipment.  Sets of limits might apply to a specific temperature, or season for example. A set of limits may contain different severities of limit levels that would apply to the same equipment. The set may contain limits of different types such as apparent power and current limits or high and low voltage limits  that are logically applied together as a set.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimitType
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment: The operational meaning of a category of limits.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.label: OperationalLimitDirectionKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OperationalLim.comment: The direction attribute describes the side of  a limit that is a violation.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OrdinaryPowerTran.label: OrdinaryPowerTransferCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OrdinaryPowerTran.comment: Power transfer corridor defined for normal operating network.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Organisation.label: Organisation
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Organisation.comment: Organisation that might have roles as utility, contractor, supplier, manufacturer, customer, etc.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OrganisationRo.label: OrganisationRole
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#OrganisationRo.comment: Identifies a way in which an organisation may participate in the utility enterprise (e.g., customer, manufacturer, etc).

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinatio.label: OutageCoordinationRegion
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinatio.comment: A region that has a common organisation or service responsible for outage planning and coordination and its impact on grid operation.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinator.label: OutageCoordinator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinator.comment: A role that coordinates the planned availability status of relevant power system equipment to meet the need by the asset owner or operator and the security of the power system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutagePlanningAge.label: OutagePlanningAgent
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OutagePlanningAge.comment: An entity with the task of planning the availability status of a relevant power generating module, a relevant demand facility or a relevant grid element.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.label: OverlappingZone
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.comment: A collection of all the overlapping cross border assessed elements which have the same sets of impacted and impacting regions.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PhaseControlFunct.label: PhaseControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PhaseControlFunct.comment: Phase control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminal.label: PinTerminal
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminal.comment: Input pin associated with a Terminal. It is used for comparison.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminalKind.label: PinTerminalKind
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminalKind.comment: The kind of quantities that can serve as an input value for the pin.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalCh.label: PowerElectricalChemicalUnit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalCh.comment: A unit capable of either generating electrical energy from chemical reactions or using electrical energy to cause chemical reactions.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalCh.label: PowerElectricalChemicalUnitKind
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalCh.comment: Kind of power electrical chemical unit.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsM.label: PowerElectronicsMarineUnit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsM.comment: A unit that capture energy from marine sources, e.g. waves, for generating electrical power.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PowerElectroni.label: PowerElectronicsUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PowerElectroni.comment: A generating unit or battery or aggregation that connects to the AC network using power electronics rather than rotating machines.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerFactorContro.label: PowerFactorControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerFactorContro.comment: Power factor control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target power factor.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerPlantControl.label: PowerPlantController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerPlantControl.comment: Power plant controller is controlling the equipment of a power plant.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerSystemOrgani.label: PowerSystemOrganisationRole
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerSystemOrgani.comment: A role that is responsible for the functional operational of a power system resource.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PowerSystemRes.label: PowerSystemResource
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PowerSystemRes.comment: A power system resource (PSR) can be an item of equipment such as a switch, an equipment container containing many individual items of equipment such as a substation, or an organisational entity such as sub-control area. Power system resources can have measurements associated.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorr.label: PowerTransferCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorr.comment: A power transfer corridor is defined as a set of circuits (transmission lines or transformers) separating two portions of the power system, or a subset of circuits exposed to a substantial portion of the transmission exchange between two parts of the system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransformerC.label: PowerTransformerCircuit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransformerC.comment: A power transformer circuit is a circuit that has at least one PowerTransformer and may or may not include related switching and/or auxiliary equipment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PropertyReference.label: PropertyReference
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PropertyReference.comment: The reference to a class and one of its properties.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ProportionalEnerg.label: ProportionalEnergyComponent
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ProportionalEnerg.comment: Serves for grouping components within an energy group, with proportional active power allocation to all components.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PTCTriggeredEquip.label: PTCTriggeredEquipment
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#PTCTriggeredEquip.comment: Power Transfer Corridor triggered equipment connects the equipment that will create the exceptional power transfer corridor when taking out of service. e.g. A system with three lines gets an exceptional power transfer corridor when one of the lines is taken out of service.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ReactiveCapabi.label: ReactiveCapabilityCurve
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#ReactiveCapabi.comment: Reactive power rating envelope versus the synchronous machine's active power, in both the generating and motoring modes. For each active power value there is a corresponding high and low reactive power limit  value. Typically there will be a separate curve for each coolant condition, such as hydrogen pressure.  The Y1 axis values represent reactive minimum and the Y2 axis values represent reactive maximum.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Temperature.label: Temperature
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Temperature.comment: Value of temperature in degrees Celsius.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Voltage.label: Voltage
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Voltage.comment: Electrical voltage, can be both AC and DC.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ReactivePowerCont.label: ReactivePowerControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ReactivePowerCont.comment: Reactive power control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target reactive power.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RecoveryOverloadL.label: RecoveryOverloadLimitCurve
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RecoveryOverloadL.comment: The relation between the recovery time and an overload limit.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#Region.label: Region
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#Region.comment: A region where the system operator belongs to.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#RegulatingCond.label: RegulatingCondEq
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#RegulatingCond.comment: A type of conducting equipment that can regulate a quantity (i.e. voltage or flow) at a specific point in the network.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Reservoir.label: Reservoir
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Reservoir.comment: A water storage facility within a hydro system, including: ponds, lakes, lagoons, and rivers. The storage is usually behind some type of dam.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RotatingMachineCo.label: RotatingMachineController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#RotatingMachineCo.comment: Rotating machine controller is controlling the equipment which may be used as a generator or motor.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResource.label: ScheduleResource
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResource.comment: A schedule resource is a market-based method for handling participation of small units, particularly located on the lower voltage level that is controlled by a Distributed System Operator (DSO). It is a collection of units that can operate in the market by providing bids, offers and a resulting committed operational schedule for the collection.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingArea.label: SchedulingArea
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingArea.comment: An area where production and/or consumption of energy can be forecasted, scheduled and measured. The area is operated by only one system operator, typically a Transmission System Operator (TSO). The area can consist of a sub area, which has the same definition as the main area, but it can be operated by another system operator (typically Distributed System Operator (DSO) or a Closed Distributed System Operator (CDSO)). This includes microgrid concept. A substation is the smallest grouping that can be included in the area. The area size should be considered in terms of the possibility of accumulated reading (settlement metering) and the capability of operating as an island.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SecurityCoordinat.label: SecurityCoordinator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SecurityCoordinat.comment: A role that coordinates the relevant remedial actions and their optimisation to ensure efficient use to achieve required operational security of the power system.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SolarRadiationDep.label: SolarRadiationDependencyCurve
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SolarRadiationDep.comment:
A curve or functional relationship between 
- the solar radiation independent variable (X-axis), and 
- relative dependent (Y-axis) variables.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SSSCController.label: SSSCController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SSSCController.comment: The controller of a Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC).

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SSSCSimulationSet.label: SSSCSimulationSettings
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SSSCSimulationSet.comment: SSSC control simulation settings used by the algorithm for power flow calculations.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronous.label: StaticSynchronousCompensator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronous.comment: Static synchronous compensator (STATCOM), also known as a static synchronous condenser (STATCON), is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment used on alternating current electricity transmission networks. It is based on a power electronics voltage-source converter and can act as either a source or sink of reactive AC power to an electricity network. If connected to a source of power it can also provide active AC power.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronous.label: StaticSynchronousSeriesCompensator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronous.comment: Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system which consists of a solid-state voltage source inverter coupled with a transformer that is connected in series with a transmission line. This device can inject an almost sinusoidal voltage in series with the line. This injected voltage could be considered as an inductive or capacitive reactance, which is connected in series with the transmission line. This feature can provide controllable voltage compensation. In addition, SSSC is able to reverse the power flow by injecting a sufficiently large series reactive compensating voltage. Moreover it can inject a voltage proportional to the difference between the line current and the pre-configured current threshold.<font color="#636671"> </font>It shall have two Terminal-s associated with it.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticVarCompensa.label: StaticVarCompensator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#StaticVarCompensa.comment:
A facility for providing variable and controllable shunt reactive power. The SVC typically consists of a stepdown transformer, filter, thyristor-controlled reactor, and thyristor-switched capacitor arms.

The SVC may operate in fixed MVar output mode or in voltage control mode. When in voltage control mode, the output of the SVC will be proportional to the deviation of voltage at the controlled bus from the voltage setpoint.  The SVC characteristic slope defines the proportion.  If the voltage at the controlled bus is equal to the voltage setpoint, the SVC MVar output is zero.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SubSchedulingArea.label: SubSchedulingArea
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SubSchedulingArea.comment: An area that is a part of another scheduling area. Typically part of a Transmission System Operator (TSO) scheduling area operated by a Distributed System Operator (DSO) or a Close Distributed System Operator (CDSO). This includes microgrid concept. A sub scheduling area can contain other sub areas. A sub scheduling area leaf will form the smallest entity of any given energy area.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Substation.label: Substation
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Substation.comment: A collection of equipment for purposes other than generation or utilization, through which electric energy in bulk is passed for the purposes of switching or modifying its characteristics.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SubstationControl.label: SubstationController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SubstationControl.comment: Substation controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the use of the controlling equipment within a substation.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SynchronousArea.label: SynchronousArea
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SynchronousArea.comment: A synchronous area is an electrical area covered by interconnect with a common system frequency in a steady-state.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#SynchronousMac.label: SynchronousMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#SynchronousMac.comment: An electromechanical device that operates with shaft rotating synchronously with the network. It is a single machine operating either as a generator or synchronous condenser or pump.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SystemOperationCo.label: SystemOperationCoordinator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#SystemOperationCo.comment: A role that coordinates relevant information and impact in regards to operating the power system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#TapChanger.label: TapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#TapChanger.comment: Mechanism for changing transformer winding tap positions.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TapChangerControl.label: TapChangerController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TapChangerControl.comment: Tap changer controller is an equipment controller that controls a tap changer, e.g. how the voltage at the end of a line varies with the load level and compensation of the voltage drop by tap adjustment.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TCSCCompensationP.label: TCSCCompensationPoint
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TCSCCompensationP.comment: Compensation point of a TCSC compensator.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TCSCController.label: TCSCController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TCSCController.comment: TCSC controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the performance of the TCSC.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Terminal.label: Terminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Terminal.comment: An AC electrical connection point to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ThyristorControll.label: ThyristorControlledSeriesCompensator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#ThyristorControll.comment: Thyristor-controlled series capacitors (TCSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment that is configured with controlled reactors in parallel with sections of a capacitor bank. This combination allows smooth control of the fundamental frequency capacitive reactance over a wide range. The thyristor valve contains a string of series connected high power thyristors. TCSC can control power flows in order to achieve eliminating of line overloads, reducing loop flows and minimising system losses.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TieCorridor.label: TieCorridor
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TieCorridor.comment: A collection of one or more tie-lines or direct current poles that connect two different control areas.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#TieFlow.label: TieFlow
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#TieFlow.comment: Defines the structure (in terms of location and direction) of the net interchange constraint for a control area. This constraint may be used by either AGC or power flow.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TransmissionSyste.label: TransmissionSystemOperator
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#TransmissionSyste.comment: A system operator role that is responsible for operating of an energy transmission network.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#UnifiedPowerFlowC.label: UnifiedPowerFlowController
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#UnifiedPowerFlowC.comment: Unified power flow controller (UPFC) is providing fast-acting reactive power compensation on high-voltage electricity transmission networks.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageAngleLimit.label: VoltageAngleLimit
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageAngleLimit.comment: Voltage angle limit between two terminals. The association end OperationalLimitSet.Terminal defines one end and the host of the limit. The association end VoltageAngleLimit.AngleReferenceTerminal defines the reference terminal.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageControlFun.label: VoltageControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageControlFun.comment: Voltage control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageInjectionC.label: VoltageInjectionControlFunction
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#VoltageInjectionC.comment: Voltage injection control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage injection. The controlled point is the Terminal with sequenceNumber =1.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#VsCapabilityCu.label: VsCapabilityCurve
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#VsCapabilityCu.comment: The P-Q capability curve for a voltage source converter, with P on X-axis and Qmin and Qmax on Y1-axis and Y2-axis.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#VsConverter.label: VsConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#VsConverter.comment: DC side of the voltage source converter (VSC).

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.label: IRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#IRI.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as rdf:resource in RDFXML.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.label: Date
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Date.comment: Date as "yyyy-mm-dd", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-dd(+/-)hh:mm".

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DateTime.label: DateTime
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DateTime.comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringFixedLanguage
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.label: StringIRI
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#Strin.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.label: URL
http://iec.ch/TC57/ns/CIM/prof-cim#URL.comment: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL), colloquially termed a web address, is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. A URL is a specific type of Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), although many people use the two terms interchangeably.URLs occur most commonly to reference web pages (http), but are also used for file transfer (ftp), email (mailto), database access (JDBC), and many other applications.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Fault.comment: Abnormal condition causing current flow through conducting equipment, such as caused by equipment failure or short circuits from objects not typically modelled (for example, a tree falling on a line).

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Duration.label: Duration
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Duration.comment: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PhaseConnected.label: PhaseConnectedFaultKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PhaseConnected.comment: The type of fault connection among phases.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PhaseCode.label: PhaseCode
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#PhaseCode.comment:
An unordered enumeration of phase identifiers.  Allows designation of phases for both transmission and distribution equipment, circuits and loads.   The enumeration, by itself, does not describe how the phases are connected together or connected to ground.  Ground is not explicitly denoted as a phase.
Residential and small commercial loads are often served from single-phase, or split-phase, secondary circuits. For the example of s12N, phases 1 and 2 refer to hot wires that are 180 degrees out of phase, while N refers to the neutral wire. Through single-phase transformer connections, these secondary circuits may be served from one or two of the primary phases A, B, and C. For three-phase loads, use the A, B, C phase codes instead of s12N.
The integer values are from IEC 61968-9 to support revenue metering applications.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Integer.label: Integer
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Integer.comment: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FaultCategoryKind.label: FaultCategoryKind
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#FaultCategoryKind.comment: The available kinds of fault categories.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#DateTime.comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Boolean.label: Boolean
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#Boolean.comment: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GridDisturbance.label: GridDisturbance
http://entsoe.eu/ns/nc#GridDisturbance.comment: Automatic, unintended, or manual undeferrable switching of breakers as a result of faults in the power grid.

http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#IdentifiedObje.label: IdentifiedObject
http://iec.ch/TC57/CIM100#IdentifiedObje.comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.
